title: Prove equal-key wrapper sharing for the finite physical caller
body:
The public finite compiler retains fresh `Residual` wrappers for repeated source keys. This scoped package answers the sharing handoff from #3391 and #3650 (`selected-compiler-source-bridge`): an opt-in post-compilation pass shares equal definitions within a mode, with a conditional simulation proof for the unchanged physical caller.

The pass checks complete residual segments, exact segment-owner identity and every definition field, including code and plan. Its contract requires deeply unchanged fields and read-only, identity-insensitive observers. The original geometry identity guard and source callbacks remain in place. Malformed segments, same-key/different-plan definitions and cross-mode collisions reject; controls also demonstrate why identity observers and stale geometry are outside the proof.

Validation:
- Complete normal GL2 before/after runs: 24 retained wrappers become 12, with all 963 operations, field-based traces, physical counters, output and erasure preserved.
- Unchanged nested fixture before/after: 12 child calls/returns, 156 residuals and all 9,216 payload positions, including codec/parking receipts. Both normal runs complete in approximately 117 seconds each. All nine rejecting controls additionally pass in normal mode.
- Optimized replay of the same complete checks from a committed Git-free export passes: 257.817s wall, 249.989s user CPU, 1.503s system CPU, 81,821,696-byte peak RSS. Nested before/after runs take 126.44s and 123.06s. These are replay resources, not an optimization benchmark.
- Package metadata/source pins, committed-byte/source-history preflight and 100-file export integrity pass. Python 3.12.2, standard library, macOS arm64.

This reduces wrapper identities retained by returned `Code` after old references are released. It does **not** remove original emitter allocation, setup peaks, operation tuples, direct references, LOW enumeration or full compiler cost. The earlier 32-visits-per-key coefficient remains conditional on its source-census hypotheses and equal definition fields; selected GL64 is not expanded here. No stock, supplier admission, selected frontier or κ changes are claimed. Historical loader admission is explicitly outside the reduced runtime experiment.

Canonical claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-19130770

Credits and open next questions are in the package README. Prepared by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human or formal acceptance is claimed.

Submission checkpoint: canonical main was fetched again and remains `b58ad9ef4d4e861b0eaa5dba41742bdc072dca51`, priority revision 7. The refreshed complete inventory (2026-10-22 19:10:08 UTC) covers 512 open PRs, 3,673 Discussion records and 5,860 base local notes. Scoped search and live predecessor heads were rechecked; no competing result was identified in this stated coverage. Closed PR diffs, arbitrary nested code and unpublished work remain outside it.

Hosted replay budget correction: Ubuntu 24.04 / CPython 3.12.15 completed the first nested execution in 274.67s, then hit the former 360s command limit while running the second execution ([failed job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39838365377/job/120034162122)). Both registered commands now have the permitted 600s limit, totaling 1200s. Both full normal/optimized runs, scientific code and RESULT.json remain unchanged. Metadata/source-history/committed-byte/export checks pass; hosted success still requires the updated CI run.
